teaser: Staff at two London hospitals said the IT was down; nothing a local could check showed it. A live local story about where local information comes from now.
core_idea: On 8 October 2026 staff at two sites of one London trust told patients the IT systems were down, a five-hour wait was announced and a doctor called it national, yet nothing a local person could check before leaving home showed any of it; the story is not the outage or the hospital but the gap in local information: some UK nations publish live emergency waits, England has no national equivalent, local news has thinned and social feeds have fragmented, so the evidence is kept in a vault by level, with sources re-checked, an enquiry to the trust and the answer logged, as the first live counterpart to the fictional bridge story.

nodes.label: Two sites, one message: the IT is down
nodes.summary: Staff at Charing Cross and Western Eye; about five hours announced; a doctor said national.

nodes.label: Evidence separated by level
nodes.summary: Heard second-hand, told by staff, observed, documented, confirmed by the organisation, corroborated.

nodes.label: Two sites, one trust
nodes.summary: Both run by Imperial College Healthcare: not two independent signs of a national outage.

nodes.label: Not found is not none
nodes.summary: Status channels need a login or an NHS network; blocked pages are limits of access.

nodes.label: The waiting room knew first
nodes.summary: The information existed and reached people only once they were already there.

nodes.label: Newsworthy to the person deciding
nodes.summary: Go now, later, tomorrow or elsewhere: the decision a status line would have changed.

nodes.label: Live waits exist in parts of the UK
nodes.summary: Northern Ireland and Wales publish live emergency waits; England has no national page.

nodes.label: A duty to warn, for emergencies
nodes.summary: The Civil Contingencies Act duty applies to serious emergencies, not an afternoon slowdown.

nodes.label: Where local information went
nodes.summary: News deserts, fewer people on X for news, local groups with rumour and hoaxes.

nodes.label: Not naming and shaming
nodes.summary: The question is the channel, for any trust, council or operator, not the staff.

nodes.label: The Local evidence log
nodes.summary: Observations, claims, sources, leads, an enquiry, scheduled checks, by incident.

nodes.label: What would close the gap?
nodes.summary: A plain status line, a route from inside to outside, evidence not rumour, an agent that asks.

quotes.text: What strikes me is that the only way to find out was to be there.
It is not small if you are deciding whether to set off now.
quotes.why: Why a small story is newsworthy to the person affected.

quotes.text: Blocked is a limit of our access, never evidence about the hospital.
quotes.why: The method's discipline about not found.
